pricing_theme: Moving customers onto new edition, MAU and Action Credit packaging and monetizing AI features through shared credits
current_model: Four Platform Editions (Go, Select, Pro, Enterprise). Contracts combine the edition, Monthly Active Users and Profiles, an allotment of Action Credits (one shared pool across email, SMS, WhatsApp and some AI features), and CX Services, with add-on SKUs for the Data Platform and BrazeAI. No published prices and no free plan.
posting_evidence: Senior Staff Monetization and Pricing Strategist, hybrid in New York or San Francisco; USD 158,000–248,000 base (OTE 184,000–288,000)
Reports to the VP, Market Strategy, so pricing sits in a strategy group rather than product or finance
Mandate covers pricing strategy, packaging design, revenue models and forecasts, KPIs, and institutionalizing frameworks and processes across the monetization function
Requires 7+ years with owned pricing or packaging changes taken to market for enterprise customers (2,000+ employees); bonus for AI, usage-based or consumption monetization
Screening questions ask how many companies you have built pricing for and whether your last role was in-house or consulting

news.summary: On Braze's Q2 call, the CFO cited ongoing pricing and packaging transitions (including professional-services packaging) that may cause short-term swings in margins and revenue mix; the CEO said AI monetization is still early, with paid BrazeAI adoption at about one-third of large customers.

interpretation: Braze is partway through a packaging migration from MAU-based editions to a hybrid of editions plus a shared Action Credit pool, and it wants credits to carry AI monetization. Management calls the transition a source of near-term margin and mix noise, so the role likely focuses on moving the installed base over and proving AI credit consumption converts into expansion revenue (inference). Asking for someone to 'institutionalize frameworks' suggests the monetization function is still being formalized.
open_questions: What share of the installed base has moved to the new editions and Action Credits, and what is the renewal-migration playbook?
How are BrazeAI and agent features priced: credits only, add-on SKUs, or both?
How does pricing work with the existing product and finance teams, given that the role sits under Market Strategy?
caveat: The news comes from one secondary earnings summary rather than the transcript, and the fiscal-quarter labeling is ambiguous; no migration metrics were available.
